authors: B. Shi and P. O. Kristensson
title: Preemptive, buffered, or guided? Empirical studies on human-AI interaction strategies for software test case development
venue: ACM Trans. Comput.-Hum. Interact.
human: Testers brainstorm test cases with an LLM; three strategies change when and how the LLM steps in (preemptive prompting, buffered response, guided input).
eval_detail: Two user studies (N=16 vs web search; N=24 across three strategies); nine metrics on test quality, creativity, attention.
finding: Users spent 126% more time with the LLM than with web search; preemptive prompting raised test quality and creativity by over 30% and cut idle time by up to 49%.

authors: S. Fakhoury, A. Naik, G. Sakkas, S. Chakraborty, and S. K. Lahiri
title: LLM-based test-driven interactive code generation: User study and empirical evaluation
venue: IEEE Trans. Softw. Eng.
llm: GPT-3.5-turbo (user study); seven models in simulation
human: Programmers judge LLM-generated tests as pass, fail or undefined (or give the expected output); answers prune and rank code suggestions.
eval_detail: Within-subject user study (N=15) against a non-interactive control; MBPP and HumanEval simulation with an idealised user.
finding: Correct evaluation of AI code rose from 0.40 to 0.84 with pass/fail feedback and cognitive load dropped; simulated feedback raised pass@1 by about 46 points within five interactions.

authors: Y. Su et al.
title: Enhancing exploratory testing by large language model and knowledge graph
venue: Proc. IEEE/ACM 46th Int. Conf. Softw. Eng. (ICSE)
human: Unchanged coding; 16 participants, control group.
eval_detail: User study with 16 participants (8 per group, paired by experience) doing two-hour exploratory testing of Firefox with the approach or the SoapOperaTG baseline.
finding: The experimental group found 36 new bugs (19 confirmed) against 21 in the control group (Welch's t-test, p = 0.010).

authors: C. Yang, R. Rustogi, R. Brower-Sinning, G. A. Lewis, C. Kästner, and T. Wu
title: Beyond testers' biases: Guiding model testing with knowledge bases using LLMs
venue: Findings Assoc. Comput. Linguist.: EMNLP 2023
llm: text-davinci-003; ChatGPT as model under test
human: Testers give a seed concept, expand or edit LLM-built concept trees, accept suggested tests and label wrong model outputs.
eval_detail: Within-subject user study (N=20) against a manual condition; two practitioner case studies.
finding: Participants identified about 58% more concepts and 48% more concept clusters; bug-finding rates were similar across conditions.

authors: M. Becker et al.
title: Just-in-time catching test generation at Meta
venue: Proc. 34th ACM Int. Conf. Found. Softw. Eng. (FSE)
llm: LLM-as-judge ensemble (Llama 3.3-70B, Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4); generator not named
human: Engineers review candidate failing tests before they reach diff authors; authors confirm or dismiss; review patterns feed the assessors.
eval_detail: 22,126 generated tests; 600 weak catches reviewed manually; 41 catches reported to engineers.
finding: Assessors cut human review load by about 70%; 8 of 41 reported catches were confirmed true positives, 4 of them serious.

authors: N. Alshahwan et al.
title: Automated unit test improvement using large language models at Meta
venue: Companion Proc. 32nd ACM Int. Conf. Found. Softw. Eng. (FSE)
human: Engineers review generated test classes as code-review diffs and accept, reject or abandon them after automated filters.
eval_detail: Industrial deployment in three test-a-thons on Instagram and Facebook; acceptance tracked in code review.
finding: 73% of recommendations were accepted for production; rejections pointed to trivial targets and missing assertions.

authors: R. Tsukamoto, S. Araki, and T. Ishio
title: Evaluating generative AI output quality in requirements-based test design: A practitioner log study on failure modes and correction effort
venue: Human Interface and the Management of Information (HCII 2026), LNCS
human: Practitioners review each LLM test-case mapping as correct, needing rewording, or failed, and fix it before reuse.
eval_detail: Practitioner logs on 18 embedded-system requirements; 108 mappings reviewed independently by two practitioners.
finding: Most mappings were logically correct, yet 40 of 108 needed rewording before professional reuse; one early error spread to several later mappings.

authors: D. Santana, C. V. C. de Magalhães, and R. de Souza Santos
title: Software testing with large language models: An interview study with practitioners
venue: Proc. 2nd IEEE/ACM Int. Conf. AI-Powered Softw. (AIware)
llm: ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Blackbox AI (GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-flash)
human: 15 interviews; prompt, refine, evaluate before integrating.
eval_detail: Semi-structured interviews with 15 testing professionals (4 junior, 5 mid-level, 6 senior); grounded-theory-informed thematic analysis.
finding: Testers define the objective, iteratively refine prompts, and evaluate outputs before integrating them, relying on human oversight because of hallucinations.

authors: I. Silva, M. Perkusich, D. W. Albuquerque, K. Gorgônio, and A. Perkusich
title: How software testers perceive large language models: A focus group study with lexicometric analysis
venue: Anais do IV Workshop Brasileiro de Engenharia de Software Inteligente (ISE)
human: Quality analysts used an LLM-powered BDD notebook hands-on, then discussed and voted on benefits and risks.
eval_detail: One 90-minute focus group with five analysts; 42 coded statements; affinity voting.
finding: Requirements analysis and test planning were seen as most critical; prompt sensitivity, domain fit and privacy were the main concerns.

authors: M. Hariharan
title: Reinforcement learning integrated agentic RAG for software test cases authoring
venue: Proc. IEEE Int. Conf. AI Cybersecurity (ICAIC)
human: QEs judge defects; feedback becomes RL reward; human decisions not measured.
eval_detail: Three enterprise projects (15,000-22,000 test cases each) over about three months, compared with earlier agentic RAG versions; number of quality engineers not reported.
finding: Defect detection rose from 78.3% to 89.1% and generation accuracy from 94.8% to 97.2%; quality engineers' feedback served as the reinforcement-learning reward.

authors: Vijayamahantesh, A. Boloor A, E. Naresh, and P. K. Pareek
title: TestAgentX: Leveraging large language models and reinforcement learning for scalable and adaptive software testing
venue: Proc. Int. Conf. Next-Gen Quantum Adv. Comput. (NQComp)
human: An agentic pipeline includes human review for continual improvement; the review step is not described in detail.
eval_detail: Defects4J (835 bugs) against EvoSuite; developer acceptance reported.
finding: Reported 89% coverage, 84% mutation score and 82% developer acceptance.

authors: Y. Xiong et al.
title: From natural language to executable properties for property-based testing of mobile apps (experience paper)
venue: Proc. ACM Softw. Eng.
human: Testers describe app properties in natural language; the tool turns them into executable properties.
eval_detail: 160 descriptions on 20 apps; user study (N=10) against writing properties by hand.
finding: Time to write a property fell by 56% (about 626 s to 273 s) with equal or better correctness.

authors: M. Lee and M. Kahng
title: Data-prompt co-evolution: Growing test sets to refine LLM behavior
venue: Proc. CHI Conf. Hum. Factors Comput. Syst.
human: Developers label generated inputs, write rationales for failures, and accept, edit or reject suggested prompt revisions against a growing test set.
eval_detail: Formative interviews (N=5); persona simulations; within-subjects study (N=16) against an ablated baseline.
finding: Test sets grew larger (14 vs 8), more inputs exposed failures (52% vs 27%) and F1 alignment with users' labels rose (0.69 vs 0.56).

authors: S. Lim, H.-C. Kwon, and M. Kim
title: When to invoke an LLM in industrial natural-language-to-DSL conversion: A taxonomy-driven, confidence-gated selective hybrid for safety-critical avionics test-script authoring
venue: IEEE Access
human: A reviewer controls every emitted test-script action; the tool offers ranked candidates for each slot.
eval_detail: 1,705 industrial procedures; exact match with paired confidence intervals; candidate-ranking analysis.
finding: Hybrid matched the pure LLM (59.4% exact match) while calling it on 37% of cases; the correct value was in the top five for 84.5% of slots.

authors: J. B. Minani et al.
title: TGenAI: An LLM-based approach for functional end-to-end test generation for IoT systems
venue: Internet of Things
llm: GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-5 Nano, Llama 3-70B, Mixtral-8x7B
human: HITL builds ground truth, refines prompt, maps to executable tests; 5 manual testers baseline.
eval_detail: Two deployed IoT systems, seven LLMs, and a comparison with five testers who wrote the same tests manually.
finding: Manual test design took 131 and 141 minutes against about 57 minutes with the HITL workflow; completeness and correctness ranged from 13% to 100% across LLMs.

authors: C. Feng, Z. Liu, S. Gupta, and J. von der Assen
title: Smarter, not bigger: Fine-tuned RAG-enhanced LLMs for automotive hardware-in-the-loop testing
venue: Proc. 64th Annu. Meet. Assoc. Comput. Linguist. (Industry Track)
human: Test engineers ask questions and check answers against cited test cases and requirements.
eval_detail: 2,172 query-target pairs; exploratory A/B rating study with 10 engineers.
finding: The RAG assistant was preferred in 9 of 10 sessions but was slower (2.4 s to 17.4 s).

authors: Z. Wei, Y. Hu, C. Chen, and X. Chen
title: Practical research on intelligent requirements analysis and test case generation driven by large language models
venue: AI Innov. Appl.
human: A five-step human-AI workflow with strict manual review of extracted requirements and preliminary test cases.
eval_detail: Retrospective case study of one system; no metrics reported.
finding: Analysts were relieved of repetitive extraction work; hallucination required strict review.

authors: Y. Hachaïchi and M. A. Ouerghi
title: The role of machine learning and large language models in software testing and validation
venue: Proc. IEEE 22nd Int. Conf. Sci. Tech. Autom. Control Comput. Eng. (STA)
llm: RAG with prompt engineering (model not named)
human: Human-in-the-loop validation checks generated Gherkin scenarios from Jira Xray requirements.
eval_detail: Syntactic accuracy, BLEU and generation time against manual writing.
finding: High syntactic accuracy and an 87% reduction in test generation time.

authors: D. Chauhan, P. Bahad, and V. Saikrishna
title: A structured LLM-augmented data science workflow for automated software testing: Design and evaluation on Defects4J
venue: J. Eng. Sci. Technol. Rev.
human: Ablation without human feedback: coverage 88.2 vs 81.3; internal inconsistencies.
eval_detail: Defects4J with three runs against AutoTest and EvoSuite+ML; ablation that removes human-in-the-loop feedback; user study with 12 participants assessing 30 test cases each.
finding: Removing human feedback lowered coverage (88.2% to 81.3%), defect localisation (86.9% to 80.1%), and human agreement (0.84 to 0.71); verification time fell by 34% with reasoning traces.

authors: D. Rumiantsev
title: An integrated framework for AI-driven quality engineering: Scaling test automation through large language models and behavior-driven development
venue: Inf. Technol.: Comput. Sci., Softw. Eng. Cyber Secur.
human: Engineers keep cognitive oversight, architectural direction and final validation; machine checks run first.
eval_detail: Qualitative industrial case study; time measurements.
finding: Routine integration test creation fell from about one working day to under 30 minutes.

authors: A. Ganiyu, P. Gajjar, and V. K. Shah
title: AI5GTest: AI-driven specification-aware automated testing and validation of 5G O-RAN components
venue: Proc. 18th ACM Conf. Secur. Privacy Wireless Mobile Netw. (WiSec)
human: A tester approves the top-k specification chunks and the generated procedural flow before validation starts.
eval_detail: 24 test cases and 15 packet traces; flow distance and validation accuracy against manual labels.
finding: Validation accuracy was 100% on 15 traces and time fell by about 95% against an external estimate; approval effort was not measured.

authors: D. Yu. Yurchyk
title: Methodological aspects of implementing hybrid generative AI models in regression testing automation processes
venue: Sci. Notes State Univ. Telecommun.
human: A hybrid model with prompt validation, static analysis and human review of generated regression tests.
eval_detail: Comparative experiment manual vs AI-assisted; metrics named, data not reported in abstract.
finding: Less effort on repetitive automation and faster adaptation to UI changes.

authors: K. Ehab, O. Abdelkader, I. Ahmed, U. Kamal, A. Taha, and M. Sayed
title: From test specification to validated test cases: A human-in-the-loop agentic workflow for HDL test creation
venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications
human: Engineers give spec, confirm at gates, validate and correct; 40% effort, 70% accepted.
eval_detail: Industrial deployment across six EDA verification domains (18 specifications, about 95-150 tests), compared with the established manual process; aggregated estimates.
finding: End-to-end QA effort fell by about 40% and about 70% of generated tests were accepted by the responsible QA engineer.

authors: C. Paduraru, M. Zavelca, and A. Stefanescu
title: Agentic AI for behavior-driven development testing using large language models
venue: Proceedings of the 17th International Conference on Agents and Artificial Intelligence (ICAART)
llm: fine-tuned Llama 3.1 8B; GPT-4 for synthetic data
human: Users confirm/edit each step; iterations per step measured (4.7 vs 2.3).
eval_detail: Synthetic evaluation with GPT-4-generated variations and a user study with 7 non-technical and 4 technical users who each wrote 10 tests; no control condition.
finding: Users needed on average 4.7 (non-technical) and 2.3 (technical) iterations per step; 1,484 of 1,983 synthetic tests were matched.

authors: A. S. Tiwari, S. C. Ganesh Nutan Dev, P. M. Patole, G. Ponnamreddy, S. Chinthalapudi, and D. P. Kattamanchi
title: IntelliTest: An intelligent framework for agentic functional test generation using multimodal data and domain knowledge
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE Future Networks World Forum (FNWF)
llm: locally deployed LLM agents (not named in abstract)
human: Engineer feedback refines the ontology instantiations that ground test synthesis and selection.
eval_detail: Commercial modem firmware (more than 50,000 files); identification, coverage, and constraint metrics.
finding: 95% functionality identification, 92% code-change coverage, five-fold faster generation, and regression suites 40% to 60% smaller.

authors: M. Rastenis, B. Chou, S. R. Choudhary, and R. Just
title: Automated software test generation at industry scale using a multi-agent architecture and workflow integration
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/ACM 48th International Conference on Software Engineering: Software Engineering in Practice (ICSE-SEIP)
human: IDE intent capture and repair; MR review; mid-generation input only requested.
eval_detail: Deployment to all engineers at Uber (Sep 2024-Sep 2025), expert review of nine benchmark subjects against Cursor, and a survey of 29 users.
finding: About 11% of all new tests reviewed and added to Uber's codebase are generated; users explicitly accepted about 44% of IDE-generated tests.

authors: B. Ardic, Q. Le Dilavrec, and A. Zaidman
title: How students use generative AI for software testing: An observational study
venue: Empirical Software Engineering
human: Students prompt, take test ideas, critique and modify outputs.
eval_detail: Observational study of bachelor students on two testing tasks (Dec 2023-May 2024); screen recordings, think-aloud protocols, and interviews; four interaction strategies compared descriptively.
finding: Strategies yielded similar test quality (mean mutation score 88.96%, no significant differences); students who relied on one-shot generation had to correct outputs and reported lower trust and ownership.

authors: S. B. Patel, S. Nigam, and S. Mahale
title: Reverse-engineering and automating BDD for modern software development with LLMs
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Data and Software Engineering (ICoDSE)
human: Generated Gherkin features and step definitions are opened as pull requests and merged only after human review.
eval_detail: Two enterprise systems over six sprints; authoring time, negative-test coverage, and cost.
finding: Authoring time fell by about 75% and negative test coverage rose by 30%.

authors: M. Warasart, U. Rattanathepee, P. Keerin, K. Sangounsak, W. Sunthorn, and H. Dabthong
title: Generative AI in software testing education: Opportunities and challenges
venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Technical Education (ICTechED)
llm: generative AI (tool not named in abstract)
human: Students prompt a generative AI tool to produce test cases instead of deriving them only with black-box techniques.
eval_detail: Two-cohort classroom experiment over two academic years, AI-assisted versus manual test design; coverage, redundancy, defect detection potential, student feedback.
finding: AI sped up test case creation and broadened coverage but added redundancy and weakened reasoning.

authors: Y. Wu, X. Zhou, A. Humayun, M. A. Gulzar, and M. Kim
title: PALM: Path-aware LLM-based test generation with comprehension
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/ACM 34th International Conference on Program Comprehension (ICPC)
human: User supplies program and loop bound, edits prompt, inspects and updates tests.
eval_detail: Within-subject user study (N=12: 6 PhD, 5 MSc, 1 BSc) comparing PALM with a plain LLM chat box on two programs in varied order.
finding: Accuracy on path-comprehension questions was 0.92-1.0 with PALM; completion time was similar (5.43 vs 5.17 min); confidence was higher (4.92 vs 3.00).

authors: F. Cunha, M. Perkusich, D. Albuquerque, K. Gorgonio, and A. Perkusich
title: LLM-CodEval: A framework for verifying implementations of mathematical functions using language models
venue: Proceedings of the 33rd International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
human: Experts review the LLM-generated correctness proofs against formal contracts and send them back for revision.
eval_detail: Five Bayesian-network aggregation functions in 48 scenarios; Brier scores; number of review iterations.
finding: All implementations reached Brier scores below 0.0001, and proofs matched the specifications after at most two review iterations.

authors: K. Kitsios, M. Castelluccio, and A. Bacchelli
title: Automated generation of issue-reproducing tests by combining LLMs and search-based testing
venue: Proceedings of the 40th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE)
human: Maintainers judge proposed tests on PRs; 6/11 valid.
eval_detail: Three-month in-vivo deployment of a bot on three Mozilla repositories (32 pull requests); maintainers judged each proposed test.
finding: Maintainers judged 6 of 11 proposed tests to be valid issue-reproducing tests, and 2 were added to the test suites.

authors: T. Lyu, U. D. Atmojo, and V. Vyatkin
title: LLM4VC: Harnessing large language models for virtual commissioning of IEC 61499 automation systems
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE International Symposium on Industrial Electronics (ISIE)
human: Engineers approve the sequence of operations and the cause-and-effect matrix and write the prompts from which the expected behaviour is built.
eval_detail: Demonstration on a four-controller conveyor system with injected faults.
finding: The agent analysed about 12,000 log lines in about 38 s per test and found most injected faults.

authors: B. Steininger, C. Papamichail, D. Stark, D. Nickovic, and A. Gambi
title: Automatically generating content for testing autonomous vehicles from user descriptions
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/ACM 47th International Conference on Software Engineering: New Ideas and Emerging Results (ICSE-NIER)
human: Testers describe the road scenario they need in natural language, and the tool turns it into a 3D road for simulation.
eval_detail: Initial evaluation with a focused user study with AV testing experts.
finding: Generated roads matched user descriptions, with room for improvement.

authors: M. Ayli, Y. Bakouny, N. Jalloul, H. Seifeddine, and R. Kilany
title: AI-driven test generation from natural language: A gamified framework for automated UI testing
venue: Proceedings of the 24th International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications (ICMLA)
human: End users submit bug reports in natural language, rewarded through gamification; the LLM turns them into executable UI tests.
eval_detail: No evaluation results reported in the abstract.
finding: Framework proposal; no quantitative results in the abstract.

authors: M. I. Hosen, A. K. Alif, Z. Zaman, Z. W. Bhuiyan, N. Nahar, and M. Hasan
title: AI-enhanced software testing: A human-in-the-loop approach for precision and efficiency
venue: Proceedings of the 5th International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Telecommunication Engineering (ICECTE)
human: Testers keep top-level decisions while AI produces test cases and end-to-end reports.
eval_detail: Literature review of 18 papers and qualitative interviews with testers.
finding: Testers named poor model training, legacy integration, and fear of full automation as barriers.

authors: L. Alrabie and S. Andolina
title: Towards human-centered RAG: A study of AI-supported testing practices in Italian public administration
venue: Proceedings of the 16th Biannual Conference of the Italian SIGCHI Chapter (CHItaly)
human: 15 testers survey + 4 interviews; verify outputs; rating feedback designed.
eval_detail: Case study in an Italian public administration: questionnaire with 15 system testers and follow-up interviews with 4; thematic analysis.
finding: Testers valued speed and knowledge support but had to verify answers because of hallucinations, generic responses, and unclear sources.

authors: R. Santos, I. Santos, C. V. C. de Magalhães, and R. de Souza Santos
title: Are we testing or being tested? Exploring the practical applications of large language models in software testing
venue: Proceedings of the 17th IEEE Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation (ICST)
llm: ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot named by participants
human: Testers prompt LLMs for test code and scripts, test planning text, test data, and debugging help; the paper does not report how outputs are checked.
eval_detail: Cross-sectional survey of 83 practitioners recruited through Prolific (21 countries), quantitative and qualitative analysis.
finding: 48% of respondents used LLMs for testing, mostly in early phases; the authors advise caution until guidelines exist.

authors: S. Haldar, M. Pierce, and L. F. Capretz
title: Exploring the integration of generative AI tools in software testing education: A case study on ChatGPT and Copilot for preparatory testing artifacts in postgraduate learning
venue: IEEE Access
human: E1 questionable: sequential manual-then-AI on same students.
eval_detail: Two postgraduate capstone cohorts (47 students analysed) who first produced artefacts manually and then with ChatGPT-3.5 or Copilot; analytical questions, sentiment and thematic analysis.
finding: Students found the tools fast and helpful, but manual validation was needed to correct inaccuracies; the tools did not replace manual testing.

authors: F. C. M. de Oliveira, L. Tiago, and L. Chaves
title: The influence of using LLMs on the activities of a software testing team: An industry case
venue: Anais do X Simpósio Brasileiro de Testes de Software Sistemático e Automatizado (SAST 2025)
human: Testers in an industrial team prompt a locally hosted LLM for learning, automation code, reports, and bug descriptions; some validate answers before use.
eval_detail: Survey of 14 members of one industrial test team (interns to test leaders) with retrospective before/after productivity self-ratings; usage tracked over about ten months.
finding: Self-rated productivity improved after adoption (p = 0.0193); learning and automation-code questions were the most frequent uses; some testers validate responses before relying on them.

authors: G. Lima, D. Silva, C. Mar, and D. Coronel
title: Automated test case generation in a real-world system using a customized AI agent: An experience report
venue: Anais do XXIV Simpósio Brasileiro de Qualidade de Software (SBQS 2025)
llm: ChatGPT Plus custom GPT (model version not reported)
human: A QA analyst defines the minimum acceptable scenarios, refines the prompt over several iterations, supplies requirement documents and prototypes, and reviews the generated scenarios.
eval_detail: Experience report on six functionalities (64 requirements) of a real system; manual specification by a senior QA analyst compared with the agent workflow including validation.
finding: Effort fell from 420 to 190 minutes (about 55%) with similar coverage (171 vs 155 valid scenarios), but the QA analyst still had to review the generated scenarios.

authors: J. C. S. Santos and P. Maciel
title: AutomTest 3.0: An automated test-case generation tool from user story processing powered with LLMs
venue: Anais do XXXVIII Simpósio Brasileiro de Engenharia de Software (SBES 2024)
human: Users supply a user story with acceptance criteria, select or discard suggested methods, edit methods, and define equivalence classes before tests are generated.
eval_detail: Tool paper with an exploratory pilot study of five professionals; questionnaire on ease of use, user experience, and relevance; no comparison condition.
finding: All five pilot users could generate tests with the tool; no quantitative measures of time or quality were reported.
